limitations: Bounded randomized agreement with a saved solver is not proof of semantic completeness.
rule: Two colour-4 pieces each carry a colour-7 marker run on one edge, and the two markers point in opposite directions along one axis. Piece B is translated so that its marker's top-left cell lands one step past marker A's top-left cell, into piece A (shift = A0 - B0 - dirB). The marked edges then meet flush. Markers are removed, and the output is the bounding box of the union of both pieces on the filler colour (1).
scope: Random scenes combine two pieces drawn from these families: outlines, barred frames, combs, U shapes, chamfered frames, frames with tails, and 4-connected random blobs. Each piece gets a random dihedral symmetry. Marker runs have length 1..4 and lie on opposing edges. The join is vertical or horizontal, chosen by transposing the scene. The groups are placed at random grid positions with no 8-adjacency between them, and grid sizes go up to 30. Not supported: markers of unequal lengths, diagonal markers, more than two pieces, a filler colour other than 1 by default (it can be set via the fill argument), and joins that would overlap piece cells.
constraints: Exactly two piece+marker groups exist, and they are not 8-adjacent to each other, so each group forms a distinct diagonal-connected component.
Marker cells lie outside their own piece, and every marker cell is 4-adjacent to that piece in the marker direction.
Exactly one pair of opposite marker directions is valid, which rules out ambiguous joins.
Both markers are straight runs of equal length perpendicular to the join axis.
The joined pieces do not overlap, and the joined bounding box fits within 30x30.
The filler colour is the only non-4/7 colour present, and it differs from 4 and 7.
Inputs always contain colour 7, so the output is never identical to the input.
known_limitations: The filler colour defaults to 1 in random scenes, matching all fixtures; it is not sampled.
Markers always have equal length, and both are full runs adjacent to the piece edge.
Random blobs can occasionally produce unusual shapes; scenes that fail the uniqueness or non-overlap constraints are rejected via bounded retries.
Scene construction raises an error if explicitly requested width/height cannot fit the pieces.
billing: Claude Max CLI; API credentials excluded; no API fallback
